the scaling exponents for brain weight in dogs are 0.27 and for cats are 0.67.

brain-body weight scaling is not a single function in all species, but rather is a family of functions, with different functions defining different species, and different functions defining the same species under different conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
brain weight-body weight scaling among dogs and cats is not as simple as the scaling of other species, and that the scaling in cats may not be as simple as the brain-body scaling of other species.
brain weight-body weight scaling is a complex function of phylogenetic relationships and the species' position in the evolutionary tree.

The main takeaway from our work is that
, in dogs and in other mammals, brain-body weight scaling is not a simple power function with exponent of 0.33, as is commonly believed.
the brain-body weight scaling exponent is species specific and cannot be predicted from body mass alone.
